officials.name: Aaron Williams
officials.bio: Aaron Williams is a District 4 Council Member with extensive experience in both the private sector and government, having worked for the U.S. Department of Justice and the City of Indianapolis. A graduate of Indiana University’s Kelley School of Business, he currently serves as Chairman of the Board for the Boone County Racial Diversity Coalition and is a board member for WFYI Public Broadcasting. Mr. Williams resides in Zionsville with his wife and two children.

officials.name: Kevin Van Horn
officials.bio: Kevin Van Horn is a current County Council Member for District 3, which covers precincts in center township. He holds a bachelor’s degree in Elementary Education and works at the Indianapolis Electrical Training Center. Kevin is also involved in community theater, serves as an Elder at First Community Church of Lebanon, and is a member and past president of the Lebanon Elks Club.

officials.name: Eugene Whitehead
officials.bio: Eugene Whitehead is a fourth-generation farmer and an Owner/Operator of Seldom Rest Farms in southern Delaware County, Indiana. He is a graduate of Wapahani High School and Purdue University, with further studies at Ball State University. Eugene has a long history of community engagement, including serving as a trustee and chairperson for Ivy Tech Community College and leadership roles in agriculture.

officials.name: Jessica Piper
officials.bio: Jessica Piper has proudly served on the Delaware County Council since 2017, bringing a blend of hometown commitment and analytical expertise to every decision she makes. A graduate of Delta High School and Purdue University, Jessica’s roots in the community run deep and so does her dedication to strengthening it. With more than 21 years of experience as a business analyst, Jessica is known for turning complex information into clear, actionable insights. She applies that same skill set to the Council, ensuring taxpayer dollars are used responsibly, budgets are transparent, and long-term planning is grounded in data and common sense.

officials.name: William Hughes
officials.bio: William V . Hughes is a Delaware County native and a graduate of Muncie Burris High School. He received his undergraduate degree from The Johns Hopkins University and law degree from Duke University. William practiced law for 50 years with Beasley & Gilkison LLP. He and his wife Roseanne live in Yorktown. They have one son and four grandsons.

officials.name: Liz Masur
officials.bio: I am a 61 year old retired teacher, mom, wife, volunteer, and nature lover. My husband, JD, and I, along with our three daughters, moved to Lawrence in 1996. We wanted a community with good schools and good people. We made a good decision!

officials.name: Kristie Krone
officials.bio: Kristie Krone moved to Lawrence over 20 years ago, raising her three children in local schools. She is an AVID tutor and editor, and has served her community as a Girl Scout Leader and PFO/LCPAA Executive Board member. She is excited to represent District 6 and collaborate with the council to enhance residents' lives.

officials.name: Deborah Whitfield
officials.bio: Deb and her late husband moved to Lawrence almost 30 years ago and raised their children in Lawrence Township schools. She has worked her entire career for Community Health Network, first as a respiratory therapist and currently as the Director of Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion. She was elected to the Lawrence Common Council At-Large in 2019 and serves as Chair of the Public Safety Committee. Deb's priorities as Mayor include bringing more growth and economic opportunities to Lawrence, working with public safety officials to keep our city safe, and making city spending more equitable so that we can effectively serve all of Lawrence—no matter your neighborhood or income.
